report.tagline: India's original digital payments app, now a profitable money app for consumers and shops after surviving the 2024 Payments Bank crisis.
report.simpleSummary: Paytm is an app for paying with UPI, paying bills, booking tickets, and getting loans and investments. For shops, it is best known for the Soundbox, a speaker that says out loud when a payment arrives. In 2024 India's central bank stopped its sister company, Paytm Payments Bank, from taking new deposits, and in 2026 cancelled that bank's licence. Paytm moved users to partner banks, cut costs and is now making a profit again.

overview.whatItDoes: Paytm offers UPI payments, bill payments, travel and movie tickets, and access to loans, insurance and stock investing for consumers. For merchants it sells Soundbox speakers, card machines and payment gateway services, and helps them get loans. It earns from merchant device subscriptions, payment fees and, increasingly, from distributing loans for partner banks and NBFCs.
howItWorks: Consumers link a bank account and pay by UPI using Paytm handles run with partner banks like Axis, HDFC, SBI and Yes Bank.
Merchants rent a Soundbox or card machine for a monthly fee and get instant voice alerts for payments.
Paytm uses payment data to help partner lenders offer merchant and personal loans, earning a fee.
Users can buy insurance, mutual funds and stocks through Paytm Money and partners.
Large online businesses use the Paytm payment gateway and pay a fee per transaction.
Paytm Payments Bank no longer operates; its licence was cancelled by the RBI in April 2026.
overview.valueProposition: For shops: a trusted device and app that confirm every payment and unlock loans. For consumers: one app for payments, bills, tickets and money.

businessModel.summary: Paytm makes money in two main ways: payment services (mostly Soundbox and device subscriptions plus payment gateway fees) and financial services (fees from lenders for loans it distributes). Unlike PhonePe, it is profitable, because it earns more per merchant and cut costs hard after 2024.

revenueStreams.detail: Net payment revenue of ₹644 crore in Q2 FY27, from device subscriptions, gateway fees and UPI incentives.
₹912 crore in Q2 FY27 from loans, insurance and wealth products for partners.
A new 0.4 percent fee on larger merchant UPI payments above ₹2,000; analysts expect it to add about 9 percent to Paytm's FY28 revenue.

businessModel.pricing: UPI payments free for users. Soundbox and card machines are rented for a monthly fee (roughly ₹100 to ₹500 depending on device, estimate). Payment gateway fees around 1.5 to 2 percent on cards for online merchants. Loans priced by partner lenders.
costDrivers: Payment processing costs paid to banks
businessModel.unitEconomics: A merchant with a Soundbox might pay about ₹1,500 to ₹3,000 a year in rental. If the device costs Paytm ₹1,000 to ₹1,500 plus sales and service costs, it earns back its cost in about a year. If the same merchant takes a ₹2 lakh loan, Paytm might earn ₹4,000 to ₹6,000 in fees from the lender. So one active merchant can bring several thousand rupees a year, while a consumer paying friends by UPI brings close to nothing. Rough estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: Large field sales teams selling Soundboxes in small towns

growth.moat: Paytm's moat is its merchant network and devices. Millions of shops have a Soundbox they pay for monthly, and switching means returning a device and retraining. Payment data from those shops helps lenders decide on loans.

pmLessons: Regulatory trust is a product feature. Paytm lost a big part of its business when compliance failed.
A focused paid product like the Soundbox can make money even when payments are free.
You can recover from a crisis by cutting costs and focusing on customers who pay.
Market share is not everything. Paytm has less UPI share than PhonePe but makes a profit.

interviewQuestions.question: Paytm has a small UPI share but is profitable, while PhonePe is the leader and loses money. Explain.
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare revenue per user, merchant devices, lending and costs. Explain why share and profit are different.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you rebuild user trust after the Payments Bank shutdown?
interviewQuestions.hint: Be transparent, make migration simple, show safety, and track uninstalls and support tickets.

interviewQuestions.question: Design the next version of the Soundbox.
interviewQuestions.hint: Start with merchant needs: alerts, sales summaries, loans, card taps. Pick one and define success.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Paytm's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Active paying merchants. Break into merchant base, payment volume, financial services and trust.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Paytm use the new UPI MDR?
interviewQuestions.hint: Target larger merchants, explain value, bundle with devices and loans, and avoid pushing small shops away.
